record: Study 4 settings: forecasting next month's demand for book categories from public interest. Fixed before any forecast was made or scored.
fixed_by: Khant Phyo Wai (with Claude); the forecasting question was proposed by Khant in chat on 2026-10-13

questions.main: Does adding public-interest signals to a model that already knows a category's own demand history improve one-month-ahead forecasts of that category's demand?
questions.secondary_interest_flow: Can next month's interest in a category (the flow of a trend) be forecast from its own recent history?
questions.secondary_tone: Does GDELT tone add to interest volume in the forecasts?

units.categories: taxonomy v3 nodes at the narrow and middle levels (broad descriptive only)
units.eligibility: a category-format series is forecast at an origin only if it passes the Study 3 minimum-size rule over the 24 months before the origin month

target.main: log share of the category in the format in month t+1 (share = theme-strength-weighted checkouts / all checkouts in that format and month), forecast at the end of month t (horizon 1)
target.secondary_horizon: the same for month t+2 with the same information (horizon 2, one month of lead time)
target.missing: missing, closure and partial months (Study 3 rules) are never scored; a forecast is scored only when the target month and month t are both available

information_set.demand: demand up to and including month t
information_set.interest: weekly interest up to the last complete ISO week (Monday start) whose Sunday falls on or before the last day of month t
information_set.real_time_only: every feature uses only data up to the origin; shift states come only from shifts whose start week and labelling week are on or before the origin; the seasonal flag and hand-made quality flags are not used as features
information_set.static_inputs: the taxonomy and theme strengths are fixed (built from subject headings, not from demand); disclosed as a limitation

demand_only_D: log share at t, t-1, t-2
log share at t-11 (the target month one year earlier)
change in log of all checkouts in the format, t vs t-1
target calendar month, format, level, broad category
interest_W_wikipedia: log of the category's mean weekly Wikipedia share over the last 4 weeks
ratio to normal (26-week median) in the last week
change in log mean share, last 4 weeks vs the 4 before
8-week Mann-Kendall tau in the last week
a shift started in the last 8 weeks (0/1), its real-time label if already given (sustained, intermediate, fading, or none yet), its size so far, weeks since its start
features.interest_G_gdelt: the same five features from GDELT volume
features.tone_T: GDELT mean, positive and negative tone over the last 4 weeks, each minus the category's median over the previous 26 weeks
features.missing_interest: a category or week without usable interest data gives missing feature values (CatBoost handles them; ridge uses 0 plus a missing indicator)

models.seasonal_naive: y(t+1) = y(t-11) + (mean of y over t-11..t) - (mean of y over t-23..t-12)
models.ridge: pooled over categories and formats; features standardised on training rows only; alpha chosen from {0.1, 1, 10, 100} on the last 12 training origins (time split)
models.catboost_main: pooled; iterations 600, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, loss RMSE, random_seed 20261013; categorical: format, level, broad category, target month; no category id

training_and_testing.scheme: walk-forward by month with an expanding window; at origin t the models train on all earlier origins s whose target month s+h is on or before t; retrained at every origin
training_and_testing.test_origins_main: 2019-01 to the last origin whose target month exists (D and D+W)
training_and_testing.test_origins_gdelt: 2019-01 to 2021-05 for D+W+G and D+W+G+T, until the GDELT backfill from 2 November 2026 extends them; then rerun to the end with the same settings

metrics.primary: mean absolute error of the log-share forecast over all scored category-format-months; skill = 1 - MAE(D+W) / MAE(D)
metrics.inference: Diebold-Mariano test on the monthly mean absolute-error differences (Newey-West variance, lag 3), one-sided; and a moving-block bootstrap over test months (block 3 months, 2,000 resamples, seed 20261013) for the skill interval
metrics.helps_rule: interest helps if, for CatBoost, skill > 0 with the 95% bootstrap interval above zero and DM p < 0.05, reported for each format and level; the overall verdict uses all formats pooled at each level
secondary: MASE against the seasonal naive forecast
Spearman correlation across categories, within each month and format, between forecast and actual change (y(t+1) - y(t)), averaged over months
top-10% hit rate: share of the categories with the largest forecast rises that are among the actual top 10% of rises (base rate 10%)
direction accuracy for category-months whose actual change exceeds 0.10 in absolute value
metrics.conditional: skill reported separately for category-months with a quality-ok interest shift that started in the 8 weeks before the origin, and for all other category-months (expected: gains concentrate in shift months)

interest_flow.target: log mean weekly Wikipedia share of the category in month t+1
interest_flow.models: naive (last 4 weeks' mean) and CatBoost with interest-history features (the W features plus log shares at weekly lags 1-8 and 52)
interest_flow.metrics: MAE skill against naive; Spearman across categories of forecast vs actual change; AUC for whether a category's interest next month is at least 1.5 times its normal level
interest_flow.same_scheme: walk-forward by month, test origins 2019-01 onward

showcases.note: examples shown in the thesis, not tests; chosen knowing their outcome from Study 3 (disclosed)
cases: Race and racism, ebook and audiobook: origin May 2020, target June 2020
Epidemics and plagues, ebook: origins February 2020 and March 2020

disclosures: Before this record was fixed, these were seen: Study 3 positive-control results (race and racism rose about 3 to 4.5 times in June 2020 in Seattle audiobooks and ebooks; epidemics ebooks +0.27 log share in March to May 2020, not significant) and the Study 3 power results. The descriptive series of four categories had been viewed earlier (see study3 record).
The Study 3 main shift-effect run had finished but its results had not been read.
Study 1 had used CatBoost and ridge on LibriVox titles; those results are known.
deviations: changes after this date go to DEVIATIONS.md (a Study 4 section) and prereg/addenda_forecast/
